questions.text: A hyperbola centered at the origin has asymptotes \(y=\pm 2x\) and passes through \((3,\sqrt{13})\). Find its standard equation.
A hyperbola centered at the origin has foci \((\pm 5,0)\). One asymptote has slope \(\frac{4}{3}\). Find the vertices.
A point \(P\) lies on a hyperbola with foci \((\pm 13,0)\), and the absolute difference of its distances to the foci is \(10\). If \(P\) also lies on the line \(y=x\), find \(P\).

Two hyperbolas are given by
   \[
   \frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1
   \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   \frac{y^2}{a^2}-\frac{x^2}{b^2}=1.
   \]
   If they intersect, determine the coordinates of all intersection points in terms of \(a\) and \(b\).
A hyperbola centered at the origin has vertices \((\pm 4,0)\), and one of its asymptotes is perpendicular to the line \(3x-4y=0\). Find the equation of the hyperbola.

Among all hyperbolas centered at the origin with asymptotes \(y=\pm x\), one passes through \((5,3)\) and another through \((13,12)\). Without graphing, decide which hyperbola is closer to its center at the vertices, and by how much.

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q1
questions.text: Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on the hyperbola $16x^2 - 9y^2 = 144$. Find the product of the perpendicular distances from $P$ to the two asymptotes of the hyperbola.

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q2
questions.text: Point $P$ lies on the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{25} - \frac{y^2}{144} = 1$. If $F_1$ and $F_2$ are the foci of the hyperbola and the angle $\angle F_1 P F_2$ is exactly $90^\circ$, determine the area of $\triangle F_1 P F_2$.

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q3
questions.text: An ellipse and a hyperbola share the same foci, $F_1(-5, 0)$ and $F_2(5, 0)$. The ellipse has a major axis of length 14, and the hyperbola has a transverse axis of length 8. If the two curves intersect at a point $P$ in the first quadrant, what is the straight-line distance from $P$ to the origin?

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q4
questions.text: A circle centered at the origin intersects the hyperbola $x^2 - y^2 = 7$ at four distinct points, which form the vertices of a rectangle. If the area of this rectangle is 48, find the radius of the circle.

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q5
questions.text: A hyperbola centered at the origin has its foci on the $x$-axis. Its asymptotes intersect at the origin to form an angle of $60^\circ$ that contains the transverse axis. If the distance between the two vertices is 12, find the distance between the two foci.

questions.source_label: Chapter 11.3 / Olympiad Problems / Gemini 3.1 Pro / Q6
questions.text: A line tangent to the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$ at a point $P$ in the first quadrant intersects the hyperbola's asymptotes at points $Q$ and $R$. Find the area of the triangle formed by $Q$, $R$, and the origin.
